title: Finite direct image reflects module constructibility on curves
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, Lambda any commutative ring, g:Y -> Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], f:X -> Y finite, and F an etale sheaf of Lambda-modules on X. If f_*F is module-constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then F is module-constructible. No torsion or Noetherian coefficient-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 095K (finite stratification), 0959 (finite exchange), 04DZ (topological invariance), and 0A5D; direct-factor refinement for arbitrary module coefficients

proof.text: Reuse the already proved private theorem AlgebraicGeometry.finite_counit_epi from FinitePushforwardCoefficientControl using a proof-only import all. Its statement applies to arbitrary commutative coefficient rings and finite morphisms, without curve or torsion hypotheses. Every separably closed geometric stalk functor preserves epimorphisms by its skyscraper adjunction, so the counit is surjective on all stalks used by IsFiniteSheaf.

Constructibility of f_*F implies finite generation of its geometric stalks by factoring a geometric point through the immersed stratum containing its image. Pullback preserves finite stalks. Apply ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff and Module.Finite.of_surjective to the counit at every source stalk, obtaining IsFiniteSheaf F without any coefficient-ring Noetherianity assumption.

Obtain a stratification S with locally constant pullbacks from the local constancy lemma. At each immersion, pullback of the proved IsFiniteSheaf F supplies finite stalks. Assemble the locally constant and finite fields into IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf, then use S as the existential witness of IsConstructibleSheaf F.

proof_origin.place: Reuse the existing finite_counit_epi helper from FinitePushforwardCoefficientControl, then prove finite stalk generation and combine it with the separately stated geometric local constancy part. Repair removes the duplicate counit theorem.
